nodes.label: Claude Notes: The Two Rules
nodes.rationale: Rule 1 isolation motivated by sensitivity of union membership data (job-loss risk on leak) plus brief's 'new endpoint next year' framing; Rule 2 no-double-delivery motivated by retry-on-stuck-screen and crash-mid-send scenarios, sharpened by DevOps bonus showing in-memory checks fail with multiple processes.

nodes.label: Claude Notes: Deliverables Interpretation
nodes.rationale: Part 0/Part A weighted most heavily per brief; starter schema deliberately omits recipient/status table and leadership/member distinction as the decisions being assessed; AI feature graded on integration/failure handling not prompt quality.

nodes.label: Claude Notes: Stack Decisions
nodes.rationale: Django+DRF+Postgres chosen as brief's stated preference for fastest reviewer read; Next.js chosen over Flutter on familiarity given equal scoring.

nodes.label: Claude Notes: Part 0 Requirements Draft
nodes.rationale: Flags RSVP-vs-acknowledgment as a genuine judgment call since Denise's real need may be a headcount (RSVP) rather than just an ack.

nodes.label: Claude Notes: Data Model Direction
nodes.rationale: Core idea: a send is N individual recipient rows, not one message to a group; this is what enables independent status tracking, resumable sends, and idempotency.

nodes.label: Claude Notes: Idempotency Direction
nodes.rationale: Any check held in one process's memory is disqualified because it silently breaks with a second instance behind a load balancer.

nodes.label: Claude Notes: Isolation Direction
nodes.rationale: Per-view manual checks are the wrong answer given 'new endpoint forgotten' framing; enforcement should be default-deny so a forgotten endpoint fails closed; detection/audit is treated as a separate concern from access control.

nodes.label: Claude Notes: Build Order
nodes.rationale: Order chosen so design work is not crowded out by build, and seeding happens early because 'a careless query cannot be caught against three rows.'
